meta.title: A Sore Throat on Sunday
meta.textType: story: a talk about symptoms, with a fact that the text does not state

paragraphs: On Sunday, March seventh, at five o'clock, Lily sat on the sofa at home. She had a sore throat and a cough, and the English test was tomorrow at nine o'clock. Mom brought a blue blanket from the closet. Then she put a glass of warm water and a spoon on the little table. She added a jar of honey and a lemon. Pip lay on Lily's feet. Mia came from next door with her mom. "Hello, Lily! Are you alright?" asked Mia. "My throat hurts, and I have a cough," said Lily quietly. Mia's mom sat down beside the sofa. "Does it hurt when you swallow?" she asked. "Do you have a temperature?"

Mia's mom took a thermometer from her bag. She put it under Lily's arm and waited for one minute. The thermometer showed a normal number. She left it on the little table. "That is good," she said. "This is probably a usual cold for March." "It may be a cold, and you might feel better in the morning." "But please stay home if you have a fever." "Take your temperature again tonight, in case it goes up." Lily nodded.

In the hall, Lily's pink school bag stood by the front door. Her pencil case was on top, and her shoes were in a neat row. Pip walked to the hall and sat next to the bag. "Can I go to school tomorrow?" asked Lily. "Maybe," said Mia's mom. "We will see in the morning." A minute later, Lily asked again, "Can I go to school tomorrow?" Mia's mom smiled and said, "It depends on your temperature." Mom took her phone and sent a text message to Dad. "Please buy some medicine for a sore throat at the pharmacy," she wrote.

Dad came home nearly an hour later with a small bag from the pharmacy. "The label says one spoon at bedtime," he said. Lily put the medicine on the little table for bedtime. Then she put honey and lemon in the warm water and drank it slowly. Later, Mia and her mom stood up to go home. "I will save your seat tomorrow," said Mia.

"Can I go to school tomorrow?" asked Lily for the third time. "Ask me again in the morning," said Mia's mom. "Please sleep early tonight." Pip came back and lay on Lily's feet again. In the hall, the school bag stayed by the door.
